name: John Hickenlooper
stance: Wants stronger federal AI guardrails — independent third-party evaluation and verification of frontier models, accountability when AI causes harm, and incident reporting — alongside support for AI innovation and U.S. competitiveness.

statements.text: Development and innovation will depend on the guardrails we put in place. This is a commonsense framework that protects Americans without stifling our competitive edge in AI.
We need qualified third parties to effectively audit Generative AI systems and verify their claims of compliance with federal laws and regulations.

What begins today as Generative AI may one day become Artificial General Intelligence. A wild, unregulated AI industry – that is accountable to no one – developing Artificial General Intelligence should scare us all into action.

Introduced the bipartisan Future of AI Innovation Act with Sens. Cantwell, Young, and Blackburn, authorizing the NIST AI Safety Institute to develop AI standards, creating public-private AI testbeds to evaluate models, and forming an international coalition on AI standards.
But we have to move just as fast to get sensible guardrails in place to develop AI responsibly before it’s too late.
AI has enormous potential to boost American innovation. But without sensible guardrails or standards, it’s the Wild West out there.

Reintroduced the bipartisan VET AI Act with Sen. Capito, directing NIST to develop specifications and guidelines for independent third-party evaluators to verify how AI companies develop and test their systems and their compliance with AI guardrails.

The horse is already out of the barn when it comes to AI. The U.S. should lead in setting sensible guardrails for AI to ensure these innovations are developed responsibly to benefit all Americans as they harness this rapidly growing technology
We're entering a new and dangerous era of artificial intelligence, and we need stronger guardrails to protect against the risks

Called for the Senate Commerce Committee to hold hearings on responsible AI regulation, and for independent audits of AI systems, stronger safeguards for high-risk AI, and real accountability when these tools cause harm.
This new era of AI is dangerous and it needs guardrails. Swift action is required to meet this moment.
Now is the time to move beyond warnings and start writing the guardrails

In a letter to President Trump ahead of his meeting with AI CEOs, urged the White House and Congress to commit to independent third-party evaluation of the most powerful AI models, establish accountability when companies knowingly deploy dangerous systems, and improve reporting of serious AI incidents and vulnerabilities.

Ahead of today’s White House meeting with AI leaders we’re pressing Trump to support guardrails for AI: → Independent testing of our most powerful AI models → Real accountability when AI companies cause harm → Mandatory reporting of serious AI incidents
Guardrails on AI can’t wait. We need to get going now and protect communities from the risks.
We need stronger tools to protect against consequences both profound and irreversible without totally squashing innovation.
